item.title: How can the world engage with China to strengthen global environmental governance?
item.description: Strategically engaging can help shape China's emerging environmental leadership.

item.title: GHG Protocol launches first global standard for reporting agricultural land-use emissions
item.description: Palm oil players welcomed the new standard, which also covers traceability requirements for Scope 3 emissions. However, it does not cover the measurement of forest carbon yet, which the standard setter said it needs more time to develop.

item.title: Subsea power cables as catalysts for the energy transition in Southeast Asia
item.description: While overland cables are just as important, the geographic flexibility offered by subsea cables will have a catalytic impact on regional energy transition by increasing the numbers of energy buyers and sellers.

item.title: The Amazon rainforest and five reasons for hope
item.description: Slowing deforestation in Brazil and pledges to ban oil drilling in Colombia offer slivers of hope for the Amazon.

item.title: The Belt and Road boomed in 2025
item.description: China's engagement in overseas renewables grew once again, though not as much as in oil and gas.

item.title: The Philippine island positioning itself as Asia-Pacific’s agroecology hub
item.description: Ramon “Chin-Chin” Uy Jr is a sustainable food entrepreneur based on Negros Island in the Philippines, which recently hosted the global “good food” movement Slow Food’s first-ever regional conference in Asia and the Pacific.

item.title: Japan drafts stricter solar panel recycling rules ahead of waste surge
item.description: The government plans phased move toward mandatory recycling as end-of-life panels could hit 500,000 tonnes a year in the late 2030s.

item.title: CapitaLand Investment sustainability chief Vinamra Srivastava moves on after 10 years
item.description: The former management consultant has been replaced by a renewable energy finance specialist at the real estate giant.

item.title: China emerges as Asia’s biggest investor in LNG: study
item.description: Public finance institutions globally have directed nearly US$22 billion into liquified natural gas projects between 2013 and 2025, leveraging green financing frameworks to tag 36 per cent of it as environment-friendly investments.

item.title: Taiwan to launch campus-focused food waste drive under new national reduction plan
item.description: The campaign aims to map food losses from farm to household as daily waste tops 2,000 tonnes.
